newsitem.title: FRANCE: French central bank head to weigh problems of poor.
newsitem.headline: French central bank head to weigh problems of poor.

text.p: French central bank governor Jean-Claude Trichet met anti-poverty groups on Friday and agreed to study how to make the banking system friendlier to the poor, the organisations said.

Trichet also agreed to annual meetings with anti-poverty activists in the future to discuss ways the Bank of France can combat poverty, unemployment and social exclusion, the groups said in a joint statement.

"The governor agreed to carefully consider...the possiblity of free banking as well as ways to assure that poor people continue to receive their state benefits should their bank accounts be seized or frozen," the joint statement said.

The meeting took place a day after some 200 protesters, including ex-bishop Jacques Gaillot, crammed into the Bank of France's Paris headquarters to accuse the central bank of causing poverty with its free-market policies.
The protesters had initially threatened to occupy the bank's offices but left after a few hours when they were promised a meeting with Trichet on Friday.
The organisations said French monetary policy should attempt to correct social ills rather than serve the interests of financial markets.
"They would like all European central bank governors to get together and place social problems above monetary problems," the statement said.

Among the protesters were cancer professor Leon Schwartzenberg, geneticist Albert Jacquard, novelist Dan Franck and Gaillot, a Roman Catholic bishop sacked by the Vatican for his liberal views on issues like homosexuality and condom use.
